title: Unit – 3 : Session – 6 : SLO – 1  |  Stack Applications — Recursion
sections: In recursion, each function call is stored in the STACK (call stack).
The LIFO principle is followed by stacks.
Stack is used internally to implement RECURSIVE function calls.
Every recursive function must have a BASE condition to avoid infinite calls.
The process of returning from a recursive function happens in the REVERSE order of calls.
Each recursive call adds a new ACTIVATION RECORD (stack frame) to the stack.
FACTORIAL (Tower of Hanoi / Fibonacci) is a classic example of a problem solved using recursion and stacks.
The return address and local variables are stored in the function's ACTIVATION RECORD (stack frame).
The system stack helps in managing NESTED (multiple) function calls during recursion.
When the base case is reached, the stack starts to UNWIND (pop frames).
